Definition: from G1364 and G4750; double-edged:--with two edges, two-edged.
BiblicalUsage: Two-edged, the sharp sword with two mouths, as the Greek puts it, that cuts both ways. The word of God is sharper than any two-edged sword, and the risen Christ carries one in His mouth as He speaks to the churches.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's word cuts both ways on purpose: it wounds my excuses and heals my conscience in the same stroke. A sword with one edge can only push; His word pierces and discerns.
